summary: Godefroy de Blonay was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Sylvain Lévi (~1891–1894). He later served as Privatdozent of Indology at the University of Neuchâtel (1911–1929).

Godfrey Edward Phillips was a scholar of religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Mansfield College (M.A.), he held professorships at United Theological College, Bangalore (1910) and Kingsmead College (1926–1944), and served as Foreign Secretary of the London Missionary Society (1926–1935).

Gokulmuthu Narayanaswamy is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at IIT Madras, IISc, Annamalai University, and IIT Kharagpur (Ph.D. 2020). He has held industry posts at Synergy Infotech (1997–2004), Sonim Technologies (2004–2016), and Itron (2016).

Gombojab Tsybikov was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksey Pozdneev, later holding posts at the Eastern Institute (1902), Far Eastern Federal University (~1902–1917), and Irkutsk State University (1928–1930).

Gopal Lal Meena is an Indologist who taught Shagun Sinha. His academic positions include Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2026) and Professor Emeritus at the University of Delhi (attested 2026).
Gopikamohan Bhattacharya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Erich Frauwallner. He held an academic post at Kurukshetra University (attested 1977).

Gopinath Kaviraj was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religion who studied at University Maharani College and the University of Allahabad under Arthur Venis, Madhusudan Ojha, and Shashadhar Tarkachuramani. He served as librarian (1914–1920), Principal (1923–1937), and Yoga-Tantra head (1964–1969) at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Gordon Charles Roadarmel was an Indologist who studied at the College of Wooster, Chicago Theological Seminary, University of Allahabad, and UC Berkeley (Ph.D. ~1969). He taught Hindi at the University of Chicago (1963–1965) and served as Assistant Professor at UC Berkeley (~1969–1972).

Gordon Dester Kaufman worked in religious studies and philosophy, studying at Bethel College, Northwestern University, and Yale University (Ph.D. ~1955). He held posts at Pomona College (~1953–1958), Vanderbilt University (~1958–1963), and served as Harvard University's Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity (1963).

Gordon H. Fairbanks was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Alberta and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (Ph.D. ~1948). His career included faculty posts at Southwestern University, Cornell University (1945–1970), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1970).

Gordon Hannington Luce was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and linguistics who studied at Emmanuel College and the University of Cambridge (~1908–1912). He served as a Professor at the University of Rangoon (~1912–1964).

Gordon Johnson is a historian and Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1961–1967). He served as Deputy Vice-Chancellor of Cambridge (1974–2010), President of Wolfson College (1993–2010), and President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (2015–2018).

Gordon Matthews was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Merton College and Mansfield College. He served as Professor of English and Vice-Principal at Madras Christian College (~1913–1939) and as Lecturer in Tamil at SOAS University of London (1939).

Gore Ouseley was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held posts with the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (~1810–1815) and served as Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1844).

Gottfried Bernhardy was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. Educated at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1817–1822), he held a post at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1829–1875).

Gottfried Ernst Groddeck was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology who studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen (~1782–1786). He held a post at Vilnius University (Imperial University of Vilna) from ~1804 to 1824.
Gottfried Hartmann Weigle was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1834–1838) under Heinrich Ewald. In 1838, he served as a missionary with the Basel Mission.

Gottfried Hermann was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig and University of Jena. He spent his career at the University of Leipzig, serving as extraordinary Professor of Philosophy (1798) and Director of the philological seminar (1803–1848).

Gottfried Kinkel was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Bonn (~1831–1834). He later held academic posts at the University of Bonn (~1838–1848) and at ETH Zurich (~1866–1882).
Gottlieb L. Schaenzlin was an Indologist who studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1920–1921, M.A.). In 1914, he served as Principal of the Collins Institute.
